title: 2012 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: Let \(R\) be a set of nine distinct integers. Six of the elements of the set are \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(6,\) \(9,\) and \(14.\) What is the number of possible values of the median of \(R?\)

solutions.text:
In a sorted set of nine distinct integers, the median is the fifth number.

The median cannot be below \(3\), since then \(3\), \(4\), \(6\), \(9\), and \(14\) would already give at least five larger elements. It cannot be above \(9\), since \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(6\), and \(9\) would already give at least five smaller elements.

Each integer from \(3\) through \(9\) can be made the median by choosing the three missing integers appropriately. Therefore there are \(7\) possible medians. Thus, the answer is D .
hints: The median is the fifth number after sorting the nine integers.
Test which integers from \(3\) through \(9\) can occupy the fifth position.
